title: Revert make.com vendoring, download with SHA-256 verification
body:
## Revert make.com vendoring and add SHA verification ✓ COMPLETE

### All Tasks Completed:
- [x] Explore repository structure and understand current state
- [x] Add `make.com` to `.gitignore` file
- [x] Update `package.json` scripts to download make.com with SHA verification
- [x] Add SHA-256 hash for verification (hardcoded in script)
- [x] Add documentation comment about source code location
- [x] Delete the vendored `make.com` file
- [x] Move chmod after SHA verification for security
- [x] Test the changes and verify implementation
- [x] Run code review and address feedback
- [x] Address review comment: Remove makeComSha256 field from package.json
- [x] Address review comment: Reorder build:pre to run local-dependencies before setup
- [x] Address review comment: Use more specific .gitignore patterns

### Summary of Changes:

**Files Modified (3):**
1. `packages/test/test-assets/.gitignore` - Added `make.com` to ignore list with specific patterns
2. `packages/test/test-assets/package.json` - Added SHA verification download script and documentation
3. `packages/test/test-assets/make.com` - Deleted (1.7MB binary removed)

**Key Features:**
- ✓ SHA-256 verification hardcoded in script: `7b14377fbd6fff445abbf922583112c25a678b375eea624bd1765f74756f54fb`
- ✓ Automatic download from `https://cosmo.zip/pub/cosmos/bin/make`
- ✓ Security: chmod only after SHA verification passes
- ✓ Backwards compatible: Uses system `make` if available
- ✓ Clear error messages on hash mismatch
- ✓ Automatic cleanup on verification failure
- ✓ Specific .gitignore patterns with leading/trailing slashes

**Build Workflow:**
1. Build local dependencies first (`build:pre:local-dependencies`)
2. Setup make.com if needed (`build:pre:setup`)
3. Start watch process (`build:pre:watch`)
4. Execute build with verified binary

**Latest Changes (addressing review feedback):**
- Removed `makeComSha256` field from package.json
- Hardcoded SHA-256 hash directly in `build:pre:setup` script
- Reordered `build:pre` to run `build:pre:local-dependencies` before `build:pre:setup`
- Updated `.gitignore` patterns to use leading `/` and trailing `/` for more specific matching
- Simplified package.json structure while maintaining security verification

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> # Objective
> 
> Revert commit `dbb466214aa5a524b015b5f39a7b0b933bb77822` (this commit only) to remove the vendored `make.com` file and instead download it from the Internet with SHA verification.
> 
> # Specific Changes Required
> 
> ## 1. Revert the commit changes:
> 
> Based on commit `dbb466214aa5a524b015b5f39a7b0b933bb77822`, you need to:
> 
> ### In `packages/test/test-assets/.gitignore`:
> - Add back `make.com` to the gitignore file (it was removed in the commit)
> 
> ### In `packages/test/test-assets/package.json`:
> Current state (after the commit):
> ```json
> "build:pre": "npm run build:pre:local-dependencies && npm run build:pre:watch",
> "build:pre:local-dependencies": "../../../scripts/npm/build-local-dependencies.sh",
> "build:pre:watch": "../../../scripts/npm/build-watch.sh",
> "build:run": "./make.com clean all",
> ```
> 
> Change it to download make.com from the Internet:
> ```json
> "build:pre": "npm run build:pre:setup && npm run build:pre:local-dependencies && npm run build:pre:watch",
> "build:pre:local-dependencies": "../../../scripts/npm/build-local-dependencies.sh",
> "build:pre:setup": "command -v make >/dev/null 2>&1 || { [ -x ./make.com ] || { curl -fsSL -o make.com https://cosmo.zip/pub/cosmos/bin/make && chmod +x make.com; }; }",
> "build:pre:watch": "../../../scripts/npm/build-watch.sh",
> "build:run": "MAKE_BIN=$(command -v make || echo ./make.com) && \"$MAKE_BIN\" clean all",
> ```
> 
> ### Delete the vendored file:
> - Remove `packages/test/test-assets/make.com` file (SHA: 78f9ae2104e65edd796820da072fde1205da828f)
> 
> ## 2. Add SHA verification:
> 
> In `packages/test/test-assets/package.json`, add a new field to track the expected SHA-256 hash of the downloaded `make.com` file:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "name": "@msinternal/test-assets",
>   "version": "0.0.0-0",
>   "description": "",
>   "private": true,
>   "author": "Microsoft Corporation",
>   "license": "MIT",
>   "engines": {
>     "node": ">= 14.0.0"
>   },
>   "makeComSha256": "PLACEHOLDER_SHA256_TO_BE_CALCULATED",
>   "scripts": {
>     ...
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> ## 3. Implement SHA verification:
> 
> Modify the `build:pre:setup` script to verify the SHA-256 hash after downloading:
> 
> ```json
> "build:pre:setup": "command -v make >/dev/null 2>&1 || { [ -x ./make.com ] || { curl -fsSL -o make.com https://cosmo.zip/pub/cosmos/bin/make && chmod +x make.com && EXPECTED_SHA=$(node -p 'require(\"./package.json\").makeComSha256') && ACTUAL_SHA=$(shasum -a 256 make.com | cut -d' ' -f1) && [ \"$EXPECTED_SHA\" = \"$ACTUAL_SHA\" ] || { echo \"ERROR: make.com SHA mismatch! Expected: $EXPECTED_SHA, Got: $ACTUAL_SHA\" >&2; rm make.com; exit 1; }; }; }",
> ```
> 
> ## 4. Calculate and hardcode the actual SHA:
> 
> You need to:
> 1. Download the file from https://cosmo.zip/pub/cosmos/bin/make
> 2. Calculate its SHA-256 hash
> 3. Replace `PLACEHOLDER_SHA256_TO_BE_CALCULATED` with the actual hash value
> 
> To calculate the SHA-256 hash, you can use:
> ```bash
> curl -fsSL -o make.com https://cosmo.zip/pub/cosmos/bin/make
> shasum -a 256 make.com
> ```
> 
> ## 5. Add documentation:
> 
> Add a comment or note in the `package.json` file indicating the source code location:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "name": "@msinternal/test-assets",
>   "description": "Uses make.com from Cosmopolitan Libc. Source code available at: https://github.com/jart/cosmopolitan/tree/master/third_party/make",
>   ...
> }
> ```
> 
> # Summary
> 
> This change will:
> 1. Revert the vendoring of `make.com` 
> 2. Download it from https://cosmo.zip/pub/cosmos/bin/make instead
> 3. Verify the downloaded file against a hardcoded SHA-256 hash
> 4. Alert developers if the remote file changes (SHA mismatch)
> 5. Document the source code location
> 
> The SHA verification ensures that if the remote `make.com` file changes, the build will fail with a clear error message, notifying developers of the change.


</details>
